outcome: Manner of delivery (vaginal, instrumental, caesarean section)
cohort: 100 pregnant patients with gestational ages greater than 37 weeks, matched for age and parity, with 50 in the study group (AFI < 5) and 50 in the control group (AFI > 5).
finding: Isolated oligohydramnios without aggravating factors is not linked to poor perinatal outcomes, although babies may be born with a lower birth weight.
mod_finding: Patients with isolated oligohydramnios had a significantly higher rate of caesarean section (50%) compared to the control group (28%).
